thread:
yasmin: Quick Q — 9h layover at LHR, getting in ~23:00. Any late-night snack recs that won't leave me greasy and also spots with outlets? Also lounge tips welcome.
trent: Pret a Manger near the B gates sometimes stays open later, but check hours. Gate clusters 3/4 have lots of outlets — I camp there for red-eyes.
lucy: If you have Priority Pass, the Aspire in T3 has soups, hot water and showers. Otherwise look for Pret Express or the food court near pier 5 — small shops plus vending.
alex: Bring protein bars and electrolyte sachets. Avoid heavy fried food if you want to nap later.
flightbot: FYI: charging pods and outlet map: https://www.heathrow.com/airport-guide/shops-and-restaurants/charging-points — gates change, so leave a buffer.
yasmin: Any crowd-free spots to actually sleep? Don't want to be kicked by cleaning staff :sweat_smile:
trent: No Minute Suites at LHR AFAIK. Quietest places are usually near the far ends of piers (e.g., gates 33-40). Pick a wall to lean against, away from kiosks.
lucy: Noise-cancelling earbuds + eye mask = magic. Also order a hot drink to-go so you can be near an outlet and sip while charging.
alex: Pro tip: keep passport and card in a chest pocket, not your bag if you nod off. Also short USB-C cable and a small hub help — some outlets are USB-A only.
yasmin: Re portable charger recs? 20k mAh ok for flights/carry-on?
trent: `Anker 20000mAh` works fine. Carry-on only (not checked). Also check Wh rating but 20k is usually under the 100Wh limit.
lucy: :thumbsup: And bring a multi-plug adapter if you're in international terminals — some stations have weird sockets.
yasmin: Amazing, packing bars + charger hub + eye mask. If someone has a spare lounge pass, bribery with stickers offered :grin:
alex: I might have a Priority Pass guest from AMEX, ping me and we'll see. Good luck and safe travels!
